item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I like this unique take on SCP-173's containment and the many questions posed to it over the years. It adds a new level of horror to The Statue - that it wants human interaction. Even when some questions are answered, many more questions open up.

+1. My new headcanon.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
There are a few errors, like the wrong usage or You're, but I like it.
Edit: Okay, I will comment some more on it. I like the e-mail format a lot, so that gives bonus points. The tale almost feels meta, and I like that too. Marcus Silburn slowly ranking up was a nice touch, so was him slowly changing his style of talk. The secondary effect was also good enough to be canon.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
…Fuck. I didn't think of that. Is it weird that I thought 'drones' and 'teflon-walled isolation chamber' before I thought 'more eyes?' That's the engineer in me. More likely to build a catapult to get over a rift than walk around it.

Yeah, let's say it's, uh, space and budgetary restraints. That's a nicely plausible-sounding non-answer.

item.content:encoded: Good job answering why it can't be observed or have its chamber cleaned without direct human involvement. I'd still like to know why they can't just send in more people to keep an eye on it while the chamber is cleaned, though. There's no way 30 people are all going to blink at once.
